newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fyffes hopes for better banana prices in '97.
newsitem.headline: Fyffes hopes for better banana prices in '97.

text.p: Fruit and vegetable distribution group Fyffes Plc said on Monday that it hoped to see better banana prices in the current financial year as increased imports by China helped absorb supply.
"Going into 1997, maybe we can see an increase in prices. They went down in 1996 and we would like to see them go up in 1997," chief executive David McCann told a news conference.
Fyffes said China had begun importing bananas to a significant extent in 1996 and could be of considerable help in absorbing supply in 1997.
"Some weeks, China has hit a volume equal to 25 percent of the total European market," David McCann said.
Bananas account for around 30 percent of Fyffes' total sales.
The group also expects to see the benefits of recent acquisitions coming through this year while it should be helped by the elimination of its U.S. loss-making activities as well.
Joint logistic arrangements with rival Dole Food Co Inc should also provide cost benefits, the company said.
"Hopefully, we will see better prices and a better cost base," David McCann said.
Earlier, Fyffes said pre-tax profits before goodwill in the year to October 31, 1996 rose by 15 percent to 48.5 million Irish pounds.
But the group's share price has remained firmly stuck around 115 pence per share although pre-tax profits have risen by around 13 percent per annum since 1992.

Chairman Neil McCann said the group was disappointed with the performance of the share price but said this was partly due to uncertainty about a World Trade Organisation report, due sometime around April, regarding the EU's banana regime.

"We would like to think that we have put in place arrangements to deal with change if change comes about," David McCann said, adding that Fyffes was not dependent on the exact regime that currently exists.
The group said it would also be prepared to consider a buyback of its shares.

"That would be based very much on what deals are available to us. If we find that large deals are available to us, we won't do it but if they are not available, we will look at it very seriously," deputy chairman Carl McCann said.
By 1520 GMT, the share price was up two pence at 117.
